sections.title: Getting more Google reviews, explained honestly

items.title: The ask: why happy clients don't review (and how they will)
items.body:
Your clients love you — and still don’t review you, because reviewing is friction: find the profile, think of words, type on a phone. Meanwhile the rare angry client is motivated. That asymmetry is why good businesses sit at 4.2 while worse ones outrank them.

The fix is engineering, not begging: a WhatsApp message two hours after the appointment — “So glad you loved it! One tap here if you’d share it” — with a direct review link. One tap, thirty seconds, done. Asked at the glow moment, acceptance rates are remarkable.

sections.embed:
The defense

Negative reviews: the response is the reputation

Every business gets them. Readers know it — a spotless 5.0 with 12 reviews looks more suspicious than a 4.8 with 300. What readers actually judge is your reply: defensive and personal, or professional and human?
Our protocol: respond within 24 hours, acknowledge without admitting fault where facts are disputed, never discuss treatment details publicly (clinic confidentiality), invite the conversation offline, and follow up privately for recovery. Handled well, a negative review becomes proof you’re accountable.

sections.title: Reputation questions owners ask,answered straight

items.title: Can't we just buy reviews?
items.text: Please don't. Purchased reviews violate Google policy, risk suspension of the profile you depend on, and read as fake to the clients you want. The ethical engine produces more, permanently, with zero risk.

items.title: How do you ask without being pushy?
items.text: Timing and effort: ask at the glow moment (2 hours post-visit), make it one tap, and phrase it as sharing, not begging. Done right, clients thank you for the reminder.

items.title: Can a fake negative review be removed?
items.text: Sometimes — policy violations (never-a-client, competitor sabotage, prohibited content) can be reported with evidence and do get removed. For the rest: professional response + velocity. Both run in parallel.

items.title: Is "review gating" really not allowed?
items.text: Correct — asking only predicted-happy clients violates Google policy. We ask everyone; a good business's real ratio wins anyway, and the profile stays safe.

items.title: Do replies actually affect rankings?
items.text: Yes — response rate and review velocity are local ranking signals, and thoughtful replies naturally contain the treatment and area terms your profile should rank for.

items.title: What can clinic replies legally say?
items.text: Less than owners think: no confirming someone was a patient, no treatment details, no health claims. Our clinic response templates are built inside those lines — warm, professional, compliant.

items.a: Everything we do is inside Google’s policies: asking real clients is encouraged; buying reviews and gating are what’s prohibited — and we never do either.

items.q: Who writes the responses — you or us?
items.a: We do, in a voice guide built from how you actually talk, with clinic-compliant boundaries. Anything sensitive escalates to you before posting.
Google is the battleground that decides bookings; we also monitor Fresha and Instagram comments, and can extend to any platform where your clients talk.

items.q: How fast does the rating move?
items.a: Velocity shows in weeks; the average moves with volume — a 4.2 with 96 reviews typically reaches 4.6+ within 3–4 months of consistent five-star flow.

items.q: Can you guarantee removal of a bad review?
items.a: No one honestly can — removal depends on policy violations and Google’s judgment. We pursue every legitimate case and neutralise the rest with response quality and velocity.
Monthly rolling — and the reviews, of course, are yours forever. Reputation compounds even if you leave.
